title: Diputació de València pilots Metalesa's camera-and-AI wild-boar detection with dynamic warning lights on the CV-600 at Simat de la Valldigna
summary: Europa Press (12 Feb 2026): a solar-powered system combining cameras, computer vision and detection algorithms lights warning signs only when animals are present; the provincial council will evalua...
account: Europa Press reported on 12 Feb 2026, from a statement by the Diputació de València, on a set of pilot tests. The provincial council had begun them on the CV-600 road, in the area of Simat de la Valldigna and Benifairó de la Valldigna. The intelligent signaling system is designed to detect wild boar near the carriageway and automatically activate luminous warning signs. The Valencian road-safety company Metalesa carried out the work, with civil works by Grupo Bertolín. The system combines cameras with computer vision and automatic detection algorithms that identify animals passing. It activates dynamic luminous signs only when a real risk exists, and it is powered by photovoltaic energy. Council president Vicent Mompó visited the site with roads deputy Reme Mazzolari. He said that after some weeks the council would evaluate the results. If the system is effective, the council would extend the model to the most sensitive stretches of the provincial network. No detection counts or accident figures are given. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the pilot as an aggregate benefit.
